reviews.text:
I own a cat and a guinea pig. This time, my guinea pig suddenly became ill, and it was quite an emergency, so I searched on Google and found this hospital, and this was my first visit.

The doctor seemed very experienced in treating small animals; even their business card mentioned guinea pigs, which made me feel much more at ease.

What I appreciated most was that they thoroughly considered the cause before deciding on a treatment plan, and explained everything clearly to me, the owner, including what effects to expect and why they were using certain medications.

They answered my questions carefully and explained everything necessary without me even having to ask, making it very easy to understand and giving me complete peace of mind.

Although it was my first time, I'm so glad I came to this hospital. I would definitely recommend it to anyone who owns small animals.

We are grateful for the care we receive for our rabbit.

Even when we notice something unusual about our rabbit, or when we're unsure if it's an illness, they carefully listen to our concerns and clearly explain the treatment plan, so we feel confident entrusting our rabbit to them.

Furthermore, the nurses kindly taught us about home care, which was very helpful. We hope to continue receiving their care in the future.

This is a very commercialized animal hospital.

I've been paying high treatment fees for my pet's visits, but my pet is elderly, and with the heat making hospital visits difficult, I called to inquire about symptoms. However, they didn't even bother to ask detailed questions about the symptoms, simply stating, "Please come by taxi during cooler hours."

I understand that they can't know for sure without an actual examination. But I'm asking for advice because I'm worried about whether there's any way to treat my pet without taking that risk.

If they're just going to spout theoretical knowledge and say they can't do anything unless I come in, even an AI could do that...

Why do they have to act half-angry and urge me to bring my pet in without asking detailed questions about the symptoms or suggesting any possible solutions?

When I first visited, they were very polite and kind, and even the staff other than the doctor were very caring, which I appreciated. The staff's caring attitude has remained consistent since then, but...
Every time (presumably because they deem it necessary), the X-rays and other tests are incredibly expensive. Each visit costs nearly 30,000 yen, and they just tell me to come back next week.

I could never consider this my primary veterinarian. (I wasn't even considering it in the first place.)

It's incredibly expensive, and while the initial consultation is good, the doctor's attitude is clearly different towards patients who seem to be regular, frequent visitors compared to others.

If you need an exotic animal examined, Denenchofu Animal Hospital is far more reliable, even though it's a bit far.
The doctors and nurses were all kind and pleasant, and my nervous dog was praised while the examination went smoothly. I'm so grateful!

The staff are all very kind and gentle with dogs, making it a veterinary clinic where you can feel at ease. However, I felt that the waiting time was long overall, from reception to examination and payment. Being in a veterinary clinic is very stressful for dogs, so it would be great if the process could be a little smoother. I am satisfied with the staff's service, so I think it would be an even better clinic if this point were improved.

Thank you for your help with my rabbit's stasis. Not only did you provide immediate treatment, but you also called afterwards to check on its condition, showing great care and consideration. I would definitely like to use your services again in the future if needed.

I'm having my axolotl examined here.
My axolotl developed ascites, and when I searched for a clinic that treats exotic animals, I was often told they didn't treat axolotls. Finally, I found this clinic that would treat it.

It's far away, but the doctor's care is so good that I'm willing to travel there.

Thank you again for examining my axolotl today despite your busy schedule.

I'm currently receiving treatment for my ferret.
About two years ago, he was diagnosed with gallbladder disease and recommended surgery, but since surgery is rare in ferrets, I struggled to make a decision.
My doctor respected my wishes and tried various oral medications, and he's been doing well ever since.
Last October, he finally developed severe jaundice (I've included a picture of his pee from that time), and his blood test results were poor, so we decided to have him undergo surgery.
The procedure involved opening his gallbladder and removing the foreign object inside.
I was very worried, but thanks to Dr. Biao and his staff, the surgery went smoothly, and he's now recovered and running around happily.
I heard that he'd spoken to doctors at other hospitals, and since there aren't many cases, I was very happy that he had the opportunity to do so.
I'm really glad I chose Dr. Biao. (He's also skilled at taking blood samples during regular appointments.)

Also, appointments are available, so there's little waiting time. (Obviously, if there is an emergency patient it can get crowded and there may be a wait.) The staff members have a nice atmosphere among themselves, they are very kind to my pet, and I get the impression that they all love animals.
I am truly grateful that they even take care of my mental health.

I am glad I found Connet.
I look forward to working with you in the future 🐾

This is a valuable hospital that treats not only dogs and cats but also exotic animals.

We always take our many degus there.

The head veterinarian and the nurses are all very kind and treat animals with genuine care.

Their knowledge and skills are amazing; degus that hadn't shown any improvement at other hospitals have recovered and are still happily digging around on their owners' heads.

They respond as quickly as possible to sudden symptoms and respect the owner's wishes, for which we are incredibly grateful.

We will continue to rely on them a lot in the future. Keep up the great work!

The doctors and staff were all very kind.
They carefully explained even complex topics about my illness and treatment in an easy-to-understand way. (They even suggested recording my speech on video so I could explain it to my family.)

I'm very grateful for the timely response when my condition suddenly worsened.

I have a dog. I had been going to a different veterinary clinic in the neighborhood, but I started to distrust them, so I decided to go to Connet Animal Hospital. It was close to home, but during the initial visit, the doctor noticed something strange about his heart, and after an examination, he discovered an illness. He was told his eyes were cloudy due to cataracts, but that wasn't the case; it was actually due to aging. He said he could see. No one at the previous hospital had ever mentioned any issues with his heart, and I shudder to think what would have happened if I had continued going there. Since then, they've performed thorough X-rays and ultrasounds, prescribing medications tailored to his condition. If I hadn't switched hospitals and started treatment at Connet, my dog ​​might not be alive today. My dog, who likes to do whatever he wants at home, becomes very well-behaved at the hospital and seems to enjoy it. The doctors and nurses are friendly and have a great atmosphere, and it's clear they love animals. Animals don't always tell me when they're feeling unwell, but the doctor is always quick to notice even the slightest sign of discomfort. It's also fun meeting the different animals in the waiting room every time! This is a recommended place in Yoga!

My axolotl kept getting bigger and bigger, and it stopped eating and moving. I realized this was not normal, so I finally found you and made a reservation.
After that, I changed its environment, fasted it, and gave it salt baths as instructed by the doctor, and after five months it made a full recovery.
I am so grateful. This was my first time keeping an axolotl, so I was a complete novice and didn't know much about how to care for it, but since then I have been keeping careful records of its droppings and food, changing its tank frequently, and taking good care of it. Thanks to you, it is still swimming around happily. Thank you so much.

I received care for my axolotl's examination here.
I made an appointment online for after hours, but I received an email that same evening, so I was able to take him in the next day.
After the surgery, the surgical process was explained to me with photos, and the examination was thorough, so I can leave my dog ​​in their care with peace of mind.

Thank you for taking my tortoise in for an examination.

It had been unwell for about a month and had completely stopped eating. I took it to other veterinary hospitals, but it didn't get any better. I was prepared for the worst, but after the examination and prescription at Connet, it has become much healthier! Now it's eating heartily. The explanations were thorough, and the examination results were clear, which gave me peace of mind. I would like to use your services again in the future.

Despite appearing perfectly fine during the initial examination, my bird's condition suddenly worsened the next day, becoming critically ill, and I was urged to take her to a specialist bird hospital.
Ultimately, she returned to the Rainbow. (I received a letter from my lawyer through the arbitration center, but it contained inaccuracies.)
They apparently keep a cockatiel at the hospital and showed it to me, but I didn't need that kind of performance. Birds don't want to live in a place where other animals undergo surgery or are sick, and I doubt they can provide adequate care for other hospitalized animals.

They used terms like "(bald)" and "(poor eater)" during the diagnosis, as if they thought birds don't understand language. Furthermore, they even emailed my bird's information to another hospital without my permission.

Birds' health can change rapidly, so please have your pet bird examined at a specialist hospital!!

Experience, clinical data, medications, symptoms, and test items differ between hospitals. Birds, in particular, are different from mammals like dogs and cats.

I still can't control my guilt over bringing my bird here. I'm so sorry, Mei-chan.

Thank you for taking care of my two tortoises!

It was difficult to find a veterinary clinic that treats reptiles, so I searched online and came across a picture of a cute clinic with a rabbit and a turtle on the sign, and decided to go with them!

The doctor was friendly and easy to talk to, and provided attentive care!

They had an eye infection, but thanks to you, they've completely recovered!

I plan to bring them back for regular checkups!
We use this hospital for the medical care of our pet rabbits. The doctor and staff are very kind and we trust them completely.

I visited this clinic because I was concerned about the loss of appetite in my pet Japanese rat snake (a reptile).

The clinic seemed a little small, which is understandable since it's by appointment only, and some people were waiting outside. However, the wait didn't feel very long; I was called in fairly quickly!

Despite that, I could tell that the staff, both during the examination of my snake and at the reception, treated all animals, regardless of whether they were reptiles, with care and attention.

They also demonstrated how to administer medication and feed my snake right in front of me, which made it easy to implement when I got home.

I'm thinking of making this my regular clinic!

[Note] (First visit) The price, including the examination and medication, was quite reasonable.

(Approximately 7000 yen) (Without insurance coverage)

My parakeet wasn't feeling well, so I called and they said they were fully booked but I could come in now, although I'd have to wait.
The wait was short.
The veterinarian was a woman and very kind, explaining everything thoroughly.
I felt very relieved.
The receptionist was also very kind and gave me information about after-hours hospitals.
I'm glad there's a hospital nearby, and such a kind one at that.
Everyone is very kind and willing to listen to your concerns attentively.
